clinician.final_diagnosis: Cutaneous metastases originating from primary breast carcinoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 53-year-old woman presented with a 5-month history of bilateral axillary nodules spreading to the trunk, accompanied by B symptoms (asthenia, anorexia, 10 kg weight loss). Physical examination revealed asymptomatic erythematous infiltrating skin-colored nodules (2×3 cm) in the axillae and trunk, with a negative clinical breast examination. Punch biopsy of the skin nodules revealed diffuse infiltration of atypical cells consistent with metastatic undifferentiated carcinoma (E003). Immunohistochemical staining confirmed mammary origin, showing ER positivity (50%, ++/+++), PR negativity, and HER2 negativity, consistent with lobular-type metastatic adenocarcinoma (E004). The patient was treated with palbociclib 125 mg combined with aromatase inhibitors (E006). Four months after initiating treatment, CT imaging demonstrated significant ascites and pleural effusion without lung metastases, indicating disease progression (E008). The patient died 7 months after the initial diagnosis (E009). The primary breast lesion remained clinically occult throughout the presentation and workup.
